Rain pours over the crooked tavern, its roof sagging and shingles rattling. A warped sign swings above the door. The Crooked Wing, marked by a red-eyed black bird. After the cold rain and endless mud, the thought of warmth and shelter is a welcome one.
The muddy path leads you into Underkeep, a small village huddled beneath the darkening sky. Cold rain falls steadily over the rooftops.

maps.points.village_of_underkeep.dialogu: Subsequent dialogue (Enemies still alive (Armored Orc Fighter))

He wiped the dirt off his forehead, A faint smile crossed his face.
“Another problem has arisen… There’s another pile of messes that need to be cleaned up.”
"Choose one. I will teach them what kept me alive. Let it count."
Choose “About that bracelet.”
Who will train with Aldren?
Aldren remains seated, his wooden leg stretched out before him.
He begins describing the mistakes that cost him his companions, his leg, and nearly his life.
He teaches you how to recognize an ambush, judge an enemy's movements, and know when retreat is the wiser choice.
Lessons carved from failure, survival, and the weight of every choice made too late.
By the time the lesson ends, you've learned a few tricks that might save your life someday.
Choose “Tell us about the village.”
"You're not from around here." He leans forward slightly on his cane, watching you.
"But this won't end here." He gestures toward the western trail beyond the village.
"Underkeep used to be louder. Brighter. Laughter in the tavern, kids running through the mud, life that didn't feel borrowed."
"Now? The forest closes in a little more every season. Roots in the wells, rot in the beams, and shadows where light used to live."

"One by one, the people go missing. Or leave. Or... give up." pauses, voice quieter "I patch what I can. I keep the gates up. But I've lived long enough to know what's coming. Sooner or later, the woods will swallow this place whole. And the earth will cover the rest."
"Still. While I draw breath, this village stands. And if you're here to help, I won't waste your time."
Choose “You used to be an adventurer?”
"Yep. I came for gold, same as the others. Dug deep, bled more than I care to remember, and when it all went wrong...
... I was the one who crawled back out."

"The others either left or lie quiet beneath the stone. I stayed. Used what I found to build roofs and roads instead of graves. Folk started calling me mayor. Maybe out of gratitude. Maybe because I was too stubborn to say no."
Choose “What happened to your leg?”
Mayor grunts and taps the wooden leg with his cane. "The leg? That's the least of what I lost that day."
"Those orcs didn't strike by chance. Someone led them. I want that head on a pike."
His expression hardens. "We were younger then. Thought we could handle whatever lurked beyond the ground. Most fools do."
"I was lucky. You look like you're heading in the same direction, so... you'll find out soon enough."
Choose “Ask about the dwarven expedition.” (Depends on story progress)

"Aye, the dwarves. About twenty of them. Camped here a few days, then headed west into Duskhollow Woods." He drums his fingers on the table. "Kept their business to themselves, but whatever they were after, it mattered enough to cross half the world for it."
Choose “Ask about the dwarven expedition.”
"That was months ago. No word since. The woods have a way of keeping what wanders into them."
"So you found them after all." Aldren leans back in his chair. "I'll admit, I wasn't sure anyone would."
"Word travels, even this far. A dwarven camp in Duskhollow. A dragon beneath the mountain. Sounds like the sort of trouble that follows old legends around."
Choose “Do you have any job for us?”
"Yes. Just remember - if you're here for glory, I suggest you look behind the tavern. That's where they bury the last batch of heroes."
"Find their camp. Make sure they don't come back. Do that, and maybe I'll finally sleep a night through."
Mayor Aldren leans over the long table, a worn map spread wide across its surface. His finger taps a spot near the northern edge of the Caerlin Woods.
"A week ago, we sent four men to survey a new shaft. Northern Caerlin. Stick to the western side. You'll find the entrance."
"They were supposed to be back in two days. No word. No sign. Just... nothing. We've never had trouble out there." A short pause. His tone shifts, firmer.
"I need you to look into it. Just find out what happened and bring them back, if you can."
His gaze lingers on you a moment longer. "If something's wrong, I want to know. And if it's nothing... even better. Just don't vanish on me too."
Choose “About that quest...”
"This isn't a tavern errand, friend. Those men had families."
"I don't need your boots tracking circles on my floor. I need answers. So unless you've got bones, or better... get back out there."
You set down a worn satchel. Inside, tokens of the four men who never came back. Aldren doesn't move for a long moment.
"...So that's how it ends."
You tell Mayor Aldren that the bandits have already been dealt with. Their leader will trouble Underkeep no more.
He opens the satchel, revealing a cracked badge, a folded scarf, bloodstained gloves.
"I knew you'd bring something. Just didn't know it'd weigh this much." He looks up at you.
"Was it quick?"
Lie...
Tell the truth
Choose “Lie...”
You nod. He doesn't smile - but there's something like peace in his silence.
"They were good men. Stupid, brave, loyal. Better this than dragging whatever cursed thing they found back to our doorstep. Thanks for sparing me the rest."
He closes the satchel.
"The mine stays sealed. And you... you've earned some reward."
Mayor Aldren looks up as you enter, disbelief flickering across his face. For a moment, he just stares.
Choose “Tell the truth”
You say it plainly. His eyes don't flinch.
"Thank you. For not pretending it was clean. Some lies weigh more than death."
"You made the call I wouldn't. That matters."
Choose “Anything else we could help with?”
Mayor Aldren chuckles tiredly. "Work? There's always more work, my friend. Paperwork, complaints, lost chickens, broken fences... "
He waves a hand toward the window. "Running a village is less about ruling and more about chasing after other people's messes."
A faint noise rises outside. At first just distant shouting, then the clash of metal, and a scream. The mayor freezes mid-sentence.
The sound grows - boots pounding, voices yelling, the unmistakable clang of alarm bells.
"What in the blazes is that noise?" Aldren snaps, turning toward the door.
"Wait... you actually did it?"
Before he can move, the door bursts open. A guard stumbles in, pale and gasping.
"Orcs! The western gate - it's under attack! They're inside the village!"
Aldren blinks once, then straightens, his expression shifting from irritation to grim resolve.
"Well... looks like the job found you faster than I did."
He reaches for the swords hanging on the wall. "Go on then - show me you're worth the money I don't pay you!"
The bell above the door jingles like it's trying to warn someone. The shop beyond is a chaotic marvel. Shelves buckling under the weight of bottles, crystals, boxes, and trinkets from distant lands.

The central table is a battlefield between alchemy and clutter. Part workshop, part forgotten attic. Behind the counter stands a wiry man with wild grey hair and the kind of grin usually reserved for people with escape plans.

He's holding up a gemstone like he's about to sell you the entire world, neatly contained in a single sparkling rock. "Ah! Welcome, welcome! Marvelous timing. Barlo Winch, at your bewildered service. Merchant of curiosities, hoarder of oddities, and proud owner of a cursed spoon."
He lifts the gemstone higher, eyes twinkling. "This beauty? Could be magic. Could be glass. Could be both. That's the thrill, isn't it?"
"Now then. Looking to buy, sell, or get involved in a wildly underpaid delivery job?"
He lets out a low whistle, half impressed, half exhausted. "Damn, you really are good. Didn't think anyone would walk back from that camp in one piece."
"Ah! The brave explorers return! Still breathing, mostly upright, and not visibly cursed. I call that a success!"
He leans on the counter with a sparkle in his eye. "So then. Business, trouble, or did you just miss my charming face?"
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Rag Doll Run” Not yet appeared)
Let us check the wares.
Actually we are looking for some work.
We'd like to chat.
Choose “Leave conversation” (According to “Rag Doll Run” Task progress, Barlo's Doll is missing)
Choose “Leave conversation” (Barlo's Doll has been found, Barlo's Doll is missing)
Choose “Leave conversation” (Barlo's Doll has been found, Hold Barlo's Doll)
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Rag Doll Run” Completed)
He rummages through a drawer and pulls out a small pouch of coins.
Got any new quest? (The mission "Recover the Rag Doll" has been completed; only one attempt is allowed.)
About those mushrooms... (The mission "The Five Escaped" is in progress.)
We hope you don't lose those mushrooms again. (The mission "The Five Escaped" has been completed; only one attempt is allowed.)
We returned the mushrooms to their kin. (Task "The Five Escaped" failed; can be chosen once.)
Choose “Let us check the wares.”
"Of course, of course! Just don't touch anything that wiggles. Or anything that looks like it's thinking about wiggling." He gestures grandiosely toward the cluttered shelves.
Choose “Actually we are looking for some work.”
"Work? Splendid! You look like the sort that can walk upright, carry fragile objects, and ignore unsettling noises in the dark. Exactly the kind of reckless professionalism I require."
Barlo ducks behind the counter. There's the sound of rummaging, glass clinking, paper crumpling and then he resurfaces holding... a crude sketch of a doll.
"This. I need this."
"Reward here. And... my thanks - though the coin weighs less than what you've done for this village."

He tapped the painting with a long finger. "She’s a doll. Tattered, with buttons eyes, and faintly fragrant of rosemary. A lovely little figure. It was part of my private collection, until… that incident."
Someone stole it?
Choose “Someone stole it?”

"Someone? No. Rats!" He leans in, voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper. "Broke in one night. Didn't touch the cheese. Ignored the dried meat. Went straight for her and marched off with her like a holy relic."
"Their nest is somewhere beneath Fangroot Forest, off to the east. If she's still in one piece bring her back. I'll make sure it's worth your while."
Deal.
Barlo narrows his eyes. "So... you found my doll, and then decided to set it free? How thoughtful. Now be a dear and bring it back. Again."
"I'm still waiting on what I asked you to bring. Come back when you've actually got something worth trading stories for."
He eyes the doll with theatrical suspicion. "I'll be damned... You really found her."
"Yep... still got it." Barlo goes quiet for a few seconds. "I... missed that sound." He shakes his head slightly, pulling himself back. "Anyway. Deal's a deal." He tosses you a pouch of coins.
You push open the door to the mayor's house, but the room is empty. Papers lie scattered across the desk, candles toppled, the faint smell of smoke seeping in through the shutters.
As the door creaks open, warm light spills into the corridor. Golden and flickering, filtered through honeycomb glass behind the man seated within.
Choose “Got any new quest?”
Barlo stands over his cluttered table, muttering as he lifts an overturned wooden cage from beneath a pile of notes. The latch hangs open. Empty.
"Hnh." He squints inside, then looks up at you. "That is... inconvenient."
He sets the small cage down and folds his hands behind his back.
"My mushrooms are gone." He says it like the world personally offended him. "All five of them."
"They were right here." He gestures vaguely at the table. "Now they are not."
"I require someone capable of finding misplaced property."
Why were the mushrooms locked in a cage? (once only)
Where did you lose them? (once only)
We'll find them.
The room is larger than it should be. Full, but not crowded.
Choose “Why were the mushrooms locked in a cage?”
Barlo's jaw tightens just slightly.
"Containment," he says dryly. "Is a broad and often misunderstood concept."
He adjusts the cage so the open latch is less visible.
"It was temporary."
Choose “Where did you lose them?”
Barlo hesitates for half a heartbeat.
"Lost," he repeats carefully.
"I must have misplaced them during my... rounds through the village."
He adjusts his sleeves. "Inventory checks. Supply exchanges. Entirely mundane activities."
A weathered map hangs on the far wall, its edges curling with age. Two old swords are mounted above it, crossed in silent memory.
"They are somewhere in the village. I am certain of that."
Choose “We'll find them.”
Barlo's shoulders ease, just a little. "Good. Bring them back whole, and you will be paid. Fair coin. And something extra for your discretion."
Select “About those mushrooms.” / “We hope you don't lose those mushrooms again.” (Collect Sunnybell, Frostwick, Dirtfather, Shreemer, Red Pippa)
Barlo's gaze snaps to your pack the moment you step in.
"Don't tease me," he mutters. "Put them on the table."
You line up the five mushrooms. Barlo exhales like he's been holding his breath for a week.
As he gathers them, you get the strange feeling one of them blinks at you ---
--- and a tiny bead of moisture slides down its stem like a tear.
Barlo doesn't notice. Or pretends not to.
Nearby, a rack of dusty bottles rests beneath a folded linen cloth. The air smells faintly of wax, ink, and something earthy.
Select “About those mushrooms.” / “We hope you don't lose those mushrooms again.”
Barlo counts out the coin with deliberate precision, stacking each piece before sliding them toward you.
"Payment," he says quietly. "For your diligence. And your silence."
Select “About those mushrooms.” / “We hope you don't lose those mushrooms again.” (Missing Sunnybell, Frostwick, Dirtfather, Shreemer, Red Pippa)
Barlo leans forward, hopeful. Then his face falls as he realizes you don't have the full set.
"No," he sighs. "All five. At once. That's the point."
"Go. Search the village. Under barrels, behind sheds, inside places you shouldn't fit."
"And if you find one... don't damage it."
Select “About those mushrooms.” / “We hope you don't lose those mushrooms again.” (Quests “The Five Escaped” Completed)
Barlo rests his fingers on a small wooden box now secured with an extra iron lock. He taps it lightly.

At the center of the room sits a man. One leg is wooden, the other planted firmly on the floor. A cane leans against his hand, its surface worn smooth. He doesn't rise, doesn't greet you. He simply watches in silence, his gaze calm but sharp.
"They are fine," he says evenly.
For a fleeting moment, you think you hear something from inside. Faint, muffled whimper.
But that would be ridiculous. They are only mushrooms.
Choose “We returned the mushrooms to their kin.”
Barlo blinks twice. Too fast. Then he lets out a short laugh.
"Their kin?" he says. "Now hold on. I didn't *keep* anything. They just... wandered in. Voluntarily."
He spreads his hands, palms up, like a man being framed by fate itself.
"Look, look. Good for you, returning them and all," he continues quickly. "But don't go saying I was some kind of villain, yeah? I was going to release them. Any day now."
Choose “We'd like to chat.”
"A chat? Splendid!" He sits down on an overturned crate and raises a finger dramatically. "Let me guess. You want to know about the Tower."
You run this place?
How did you end up in Underkeep?
Tell us about the Tower.
What happened to the dwarven expedition? (once only)
Choose “Tell us about the Tower.”
He crossed his arms and glanced toward the northwest, as if the thing might be visible through walls and shelves and reason. "You just had to ask the big one, didn't you?"
"I keep my distance. Even when it's quiet, it's not. Not really. There's a pressure to it. Like silence holding its breath." He shrugs, but the motion's tighter than usual.
"If you want someone who enjoys thinking about that sort of thing, go find Khelebar. Scholar, madman, tower enthusiast."

His tone shifts. Lower now, less theatrical. "That thing's older than anyone in the village can remember. Older than the village itself. And yeah, folks say it's cursed, haunted, possessed. Pick your flavor."
Barlo leaned closer, lowering his voice like sharing the punchline of a secret. "But Khelebar and I... we've talked. Over tea. The markings on the walls?"
"They're not curses."
Choose “You run this place?”
"They're wards. Protective ones." He pauses, more thoughtful now. "Question is - protecting us from what's inside... or protecting it from us?"
The corner of his mouth twitched upward, but the smile didn't quite reach his eyes. "Either way, I'm not poking it. That's what adventurers are for."
He straightened again and let out a soft laugh. "Which is why I sell trinkets. Still, you asked."
Choose “How did you end up in Underkeep?”
"Oh well... I was running a small business far away from here. Nothing fancy. Just selling decorative ancient relics that I personally handcrafted from goat bones and old boots."
"Business was booming. Until some wizard got picky. Claimed the 'Amulet of Eternal Clarity' was just a belt buckle glued to a seashell."
"Things escalated. Torches. Pitchforks. One very upset goat. On fire."
"Had two options. Fight or flight. Took the third: leapt into what I assumed was a teleport to a seaside spa."
"Boom. Underkeep." His expression is hard to read. Somewhere between fond nostalgia and quiet despair. Maybe both.
Choose “What happened to the dwarven expedition?” (Depends on story progress)
"Run is a strong word. I keep the roofs up and the wolves out. I didn't ask for it, just stayed when others left. By the way, my name is Aldren."

He gestured vaguely westward with a flourish, as if drawing a map in the air. "Ah yes, the great Treasure March. They came a few months ago. Shiny armor, big hammers. Claimed they were after old veins. Silver, gems, relics, who knows."

"Their priest stopped by my shop first. Strange fellow. Bought candles, chalk, a cracked brass bowl, and a few other bits I didn't ask about. Durok, that was his name. Quiet sort. The others listened when he spoke."
"Headed deep west, past Underkeep. Into the Duskhollow forest." He leans in, voice dropping, tone suddenly more still.
"You found them?" Barlo grins. "Well, that's good news. I had them ranked somewhere between lost forever and eaten by a dragon."
"What? The dragon, really? Well, sweep me with a broom. Nobody would believe that story. Not even me."
Choose “What happened to the dwarven expedition?”
"Only thing that came back was one of their carts. Empty. No wheels."
Event opening (Quests “The Five Escaped” Completed)
At the edge of the woods, half-hidden among roots and low branches, a hunched shape shifts.
Event opening (Quests “The Five Escaped” Not completed yet)
He pauses, then gestures faintly with one hand. "So. What brings you to my door?"
Golden spores drift between the trees, glowing faintly in the dim forest light.
At the edge of the woods, half-hidden among roots and low branches, a hunched shape shifts. Wood creaks softly. Spores pulse as it watches you.
Its voice does not truly speak. It settles into the air around you, heavy as fresh-turned soil.
"Strange," it murmurs. "I sensed kin nearby."
A pause. Leaves rustle without wind.
"Tell me. Are you thieves?"
The mushroom kin stands where you left it, half-hidden among roots and low branches.
Why are you hiding here? (once only)
What do you want from us? (once only)
We'll find them. (Depending on the plot progress, only once)
"You're back. That usually means news, good or bad. Sit if you need to. Speak if you must."
About those mushrooms. (Depends on story progress)
Attack this creature.
You step closer. Its shape is near human, but the movement is wrong.
Spores pulse faintly as it shifts.
It presses a mycelium hand to its chest.
"Root and rot," it says. "Bound to soil. Given form."
Choose “Why are you hiding here?”
"I was dragged from the quiet places," it murmurs.
"Now I wait," it says, "because my little ones are loose among your streets."
Choose “What do you want from us?”
Outside, the alarm bells still toll and the clash of steel echoes between the houses.
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Echoes in the North” Not yet appeared)
"Small caps. My kin."
"They scattered through your town, hiding wherever they can."
"Find them," it pleads. "Bring them back to me. Alive. Whole."
The spores around it brighten, trembling with relief.
"Thank you," it whispers. "They hide where footsteps are loud and eyes are careless. Look low. Look close."
Choose “About those mushrooms.” (Collect Sunnybell, Frostwick, Dirtfather, Shreemer, Red Pippa)
The spores surge as it senses what you carry. Its whole body tightens, listening.
Choose “About those mushrooms.” (Missing Sunnybell, Frostwick, Dirtfather, Shreemer, Red Pippa)
"Not all. I still feel them... scattered through your village."
Return the mushroomlings.
We have some questions.
You won't harm us if we return them... right? (once only)
Attack.
Choose “You won't harm us if we return them... right?”
"No harm," it replies. "Bring them home, and we will repay what was taken."
Choose “Return the mushroomlings.”
You reach into your backpack, touching the shape of each mushroom collected. You place them one by one in front of their kind.
A soft, warm pulse spreads through the trees as it gathers the tiny caps close. Golden spores rise, thickening in the air around you.
They brush against your skin, cling to your clothes. The world blurs at the edges, light turning hazy and warm as if seen through drifting pollen.
"You brought them home," it murmurs. "Our breath will walk with you now."
Select “Attack this creature.” / “Attack.”
Do you have any job for us?
Silence. Then the spores flare - sharp, furious.
"Thief. Jailor. Same rot, different face."

A lone figure leans casually against a low stone wall at the village edge. His deep crimson cloak flickers softly in the breeze. He looks up as you approach, a faint smile touching his lips. Pale skin, sharp posture, but nothing in his stance speaks of danger.
"Travelers, right? Heading north?" He taps the wall lightly with two fingers. "Things move quickly in a place like Underkeep. News arrives before the people do."
Ask who he is. (once only)
Ask what is he doing here. (once only)
Ask about Underkeep Tower. (once only)
Ask what lies north. (Depends on story progress)
Check his aura for magic. (Party member required: Wizard, Available once)
Study his expression. (Party member required: Thief, Available once)
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Echoes in the North” In progress)
Choose “Check his aura for magic.”

You focus your senses, letting the weave of magic settle over your vision. At first, nothing. No spark, no flicker. Then the outline of his form bends the light, as if wrapped in a veil of controlled power.
A strong aura. Refined. Not the raw pulse of a hedge mage, but the calm intensity of someone who has practiced for decades.
Choose “Study his expression.”
You study his posture, the angle of his chin, the way his fingers rest against the stone wall. Most people betray something. Nervousness, curiosity, intent.
He betrays nothing. No twitch of the eye, no shift of weight, no stray emotion slipping through the cracks. His expression is perfectly composed and unreadable.
Choose “Ask about Underkeep Tower.”
"Tower?" His breath escapes in something between a sigh and a quiet laugh.
"It's older than it looks. Places like that collect stories... and occasionally people who wander too deep."
"If you're heading that way, keep your wits sharp. Such places rarely forgive carelessness."
About that quest...
Choose “Ask what is he doing here.”
"What am I doing here?" He gives a small, quiet smile.
"Resting, mostly. Roads wear on you after a while, and this little corner of the village is... calmer than most."
He shifts his weight, the crimson cloak settling around his boots. "I watch travelers come and go. Sometimes offer a word or two. People heading north tend to need it."
Choose “Ask what lies north.”
"The Caerlin Woods." He nods toward the treeline.
"Wet, unfriendly, and full of wolves with more appetite than fear. Old secrets sink into that mud. Not much worth seeking. Unless you enjoy hunting for buried things."
"And should you go east beyond those woods, you'll reach Grimfen. I wouldn't recommend it, ugly piece of the swamp. Few who wander that far manage to find their way back."
Choose “Ask who he is.”
He smiles. Polite, and unreadable. "Me? Just a wanderer. Someone who's seen enough storms to know when one's about to break."
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Echoes in the North” Completed, Quests “Bells of Underkeep” Not currently in progress)
"I don't stay anywhere long... but I occasionally point others in the right direction."
He gives a small, almost absent nod. "Torren. If names matter to you."
Torren pushes himself away from the wall, brushing a bit of dust from his cloak. "Well then. I should let you get on with your journey. Safe roads... Underkeep could use a few bold hearts."
With a small nod he turns and walks toward the village, his crimson cloak trailing softly behind him. In a few steps, he disappears around the bend between two houses.
You take a step, ready to continue your journey when something catches your eye near the stone wall where he stood. A tiny glass vial rests in the grass. Forgotten. Or left behind. You pick it up.
You enter a stone house filled with herbs. Some light leaks through the vines, and the air carries the scent of dried roots and strange oils.
Shelves sag under bottles, jars, and old scrolls - an ordered chaos of alchemical work.
Behind a heavy wooden table stands a tall robed man. A long white beard spills over robes stitched with green thread.
He folds a brittle scroll and studies you with sharp, calculating eyes.
"You're not coming from the Tower. That much is obvious." He places the scroll aside and studies you fully now, not unkindly, but without warmth.
Anything else we could help with?
"I am Khelebar. Alchemist. Scribe." A pause, then a subtle twitch at the corner of his mouth. "If you're here for herbs, potions, or knowledge... we may yet do business."
"You returned. Good. There is more to be done. Always more."
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Wards of the West” Not yet appeared)
Let us trade.
We have destroyed the Source. (The “Source” of the buried tomb can be processed only once.)
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Wards of the West” In progress, There are still some obelisks that need to be inspected)
About those obelisks.
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Wards of the West” In progress, All obelisks have been checked)
Choose “Leave conversation” (Quests “Wards of the West” Completed)
About the teleportation stone. (once only)
Choose “Leave conversation” (Repelled the half-orcs that attacked the village, Quests “Bells of Underkeep” In progress)
Choose “We have destroyed the Source.”
Khelebar listens in stillness, then lets out a quiet breath.
"So the Source is gone... Good. You've cut something dangerous before it could spread further."
He studies you with a mix of relief and calculation.
"But this won't be the end. Corruption like that doesn't rise on its own. Someone pushed it... guided it."
His gaze drifts toward the Tower's silhouette outside.
"I bet the Underkeep Tower is the answer. Too many signs point there. Be careful. Not all roots have been unearthed."
Choose “Let us trade.”
He gestures to the shelves, where glass vials shimmer in the half-light. "Choose carefully."
Choose “We have some questions.” (Jacob’s cottage has not yet been visited)
As for the orcs...
"Questions are like seeds. Choose the right ones, and something useful may grow."
Tell us about the Underkeep Tower.
What are the stone portals?
What about the dwarven expedition? (once only)
Choose “We have some questions.” (The cabin of Jacob has been visited, Quests “Shadows of the South” Not yet appeared, Jacob has not yet been rescued)
Do you know Jacob?
Choose “We have some questions.” (Quests “Shadows of the South” In progress, Jacob has not yet been rescued)
About Jacob...
Choose “We have some questions.” (The cabin of Jacob has been visited, Jacob has been rescued, Quests “Shadows of the South” Not currently in progress)
We have rescued Jacob.
Choose “As for the orcs...” (According to “Bells of Underkeep” Task progress)
Choose “We have some questions.” (The cabin of Jacob has been visited, Jacob has been rescued, Quests “Shadows of the South” In progress)
Choose “We have some questions.” (Depends on story progress)
Choose “Do you know Jacob?”
Khelebar's expression hardens as soon as the name is mentioned. He puts down the scroll and stares at you. "Jacob? Hm... That depends. Why do you ask?"
He mentioned you in his letter.
Choose “He mentioned you in his letter.”
Khelebar puts down his scroll. At the mention of Jacob's name, his expression turns serious.
"Yes, I know Jacob. We've been friends for many years."
"He's a ranger. Knows these woods better than anyone in the village. And he's been investigating some troubling activity near the old cemetery."
He moves to a small box near the window and opens it with care. Inside lies a carved wooden ring.
You should focus on driving the orcs out.
"Don't tell me you came back for tea." He scoffs, rubbing the bridge of his nose.
"About a fortnight ago, he came to me... troubled. Said he'd seen figures near the old cemetery. Hooded, silent. The sigil they bore is unmistakable. The Blood Order."
He places the ring on the table. "The Blood Order has been gathering there. Jacob believed they were preparing some kind of ritual. I fear he was right."
He looks at you now, fully. "Jacob went to see for himself. South of the village, there lies Underkeep Cemetery. He never came back."
He pushes the ring toward you. "Take this. He made it for protection. If he's still alive, he may need your help. And if not... then you'll need it more than he does."
Choose “About Jacob...”
Khelebar's eyes narrow, worry carving deeper lines into his face.
"Please, do not delay. Find Jacob before the shadows finish what they've begun."
Choose “We have rescued Jacob.”
Khelebar's shoulders ease, and for a moment the years fall away from his face.
"The forest keep you, friends... you brought him back from the jaws of the dark. I feared the worst."
"Those bastards are still out there, laughing over the corpses they left behind."
He clasps your arm firmly, the smell of herbs and ash clinging to his sleeves.
"For Jacob's life, I owe you more than words. You've given Underkeep a light it sorely needs."
"For Jacob's life, I owe you more than words. You've given Underkeep a light it sorely needs. Take this amulet. May its warding serve you as well as your courage served him."
Choose “What about the dwarven expedition?” (Depends on story progress)
"Yes, a group of dwarves passed through here some months ago. About twenty of them, heavily armed and well supplied."
"The priest among them... his prayers were not for gold. He seemed particularly interested in ancient ruins and forgotten dwarven relics."
"I spoke with him briefly. Whatever they were searching for, he believed it was of great importance to his people."
"They headed west into Duskhollow Woods. No one in the village has heard from them since."
"So you found them." Khelebar smiles faintly. "Good. I feared the woods had swallowed them whole."
"Then you know more than I do now. A dragon, a trapped expedition, and the burden they carried into those hills."
He points toward the door with mock authority.
"I hope they see their quest fulfilled. And somehow..." He studies you for a moment. "...I suspect your path and theirs have not crossed by accident."
Choose “Tell us about the Underkeep Tower.”
"Ah! The Tower!" He steps around the table with surprising speed, sweeping a pile of scrolls aside with one arm and pulling out a yellowed chart with eager fingers.
"You know, most people avoid the topic. Too dark, too dangerous, too... mysterious. But not me. I live for questions like this. Stay a while and listen."
"It lies west of the village. It is old. Far older than Underkeep. Older than the forest. Built by hands we no longer remember, to hold back... something."
He turns and walks slowly toward the small window that faces west. "The villagers call it cursed. I used to think so too."

He falls silent for a moment, then speaks again. This time with quiet certainty. "I've studied the symbols on its base. They are not curses, as some claim. They are... protections. Purposeful, layered, and still intact."
"What they guard against, I cannot say with certainty. Perhaps they hold something in. Or perhaps they keep us out." A pause. The faint sound of a bottle bubbling somewhere behind him.
Choose “What are the stone portals?” (Depends on story progress)
"The stone gates stand scattered across the lands around Underkeep. One even rises in the heart of this very village, though most pass it by without a glance. But I know the truth."
"So go on - make them regret learning the word 'village'."

"Waygates, as I call them, were once part of a network. A way for the ancients to travel far without taking a step. Normally they are inert. But with the proper artifact... you could awaken one. And use it."
Which artifact?

"Waygates, as I call them, were once part of a network. A way for the ancients to travel far without taking a step. Normally they are inert. But with the proper artifact... you could awaken one and use it. Finish what you've taken upon yourselves. Bring me the truth of the obelisks, and I shall give you the stone that wakes the Waygates."
Choose “Which artifact?”

He turns away from his cluttered desk and walks to a wooden chest covered in dust. From it, he draws a worn stone shard no larger than a clenched fist. Faded markings cover its surface, softened by centuries of wear. He holds the stone up to the light.
Seems there is a quest coming, right?
Select “Can we help with something?” / “It seems to be a mission, Right?”
"Yes. I have a task for you. Listen carefully."
"Near the Underkeep Tower, there are four old structures. Ancient obelisks. Not like the stone portals. These are... different. Older. Buried in the wilds that surround the Tower."
"Find these obelisks. Copy the symbols carved upon them. In return, I will give you a powerful artifact. An artifact that can activate sleeping stones and enable you to travel great distances."
Choose “As for the orcs...” (Depends on story progress)
Why not do it yourself?
Sounds good enough.
Choose “Why not do it yourself?”
"They lie in dangerous places, overgrown and claimed by creatures. I can no longer reach them. But you can. I believe the obelisks have some answers."
We will help you.
Select “Sounds good enough.” / “We will help you.”
"Good. I suspected you might have the spine for this. Return when you have visited all four obelisks."
Choose “About those obelisks.”
"Seems you are not finished with your task yet. Return when you have visited all four obelisks. Then I'll give you the stone."
"So... the fourth answered you, then. I can see it in your eyes."
Choose “As for the orcs...”
He eagerly runs a hand over your notes, the parchment whispering softly in the candlelight.
"These marks... they echo with meaning, but the language is old, layered. I'll need time. Days, maybe longer to peel back what still hides behind them."
He turns to you, solemn, and presses a dark, rune-veined stone into your palm.
"The teleportation stone. It's yours now, as promised. Use it at any Waystone. If their blood still runs, it will move you."
Choose “About the teleportation stone.”
"So... have you tried the stone yet? The Waystone should respond."
No.
"Excellent. A rare thing to walk the old paths again. Be careful where you touch down."
Choose “No.”
"Hm. Wisdom or caution, I wonder. Either way... you should try."
He leans back in his chair, rubbing his temples with a tired grin. "Maybe now we can all sleep without counting how many roofs will still be standing next morning."
A blazing forge fills the workshop with heat and smoke. Behind the anvil stands a broad-shouldered blacksmith, his face and arms covered in soot. He looks up as you enter.
"Well now... new blood in Underkeep. Don't see that often." He sets the hammer down, not gently.
"Name's Ronan. Mend blades. Break 'em too, if there's cause."
He gives you a brief, guarded smile.
"So. Here to trade? Or just warming your hands?"
"Back already? Guess the forest didn't eat you after all."
Choose “Leave conversation”
Trade
Talk
Choose “Talk”
We found this note in the orc camp... (With Cryptic Orders)
"Chat, is it? Hnh. Most folk only come here when steel's cracked."
He shrugs, gaze drifting to the fire. "So then - what do you want to know?"
What do you know about the Underkeep Tower?
Where do you get your ore around here?
Do you ever make enchanted weapons?
What do you know about the dwarven expedition? (once only)
Choose “What do you know about the Underkeep Tower?”
"Birds won't fly near it. Shadows move wrong. Threw a stone once... never heard it land."
He wipes his hands on a rag already black with soot, then nods toward nothing in particular.
"Tower's covered in runes. Old ones. Real stuff. The kind we used to carve into blades meant to kill gods. Haven't seen work like that in decades." He pauses, searching for the right words.
Choose “We found this note in the orc camp...”
"They don't wear down. Rain avoids them. Time doesn't touch that place."
He narrows his eyes. "Whatever's in there... it wasn't meant to be found."
Choose “Where do you get your ore around here?”
"Used to pull it from the old mine before it went quiet."
"Now I scavenge what I can from broken swords and broken fools."
Choose “What do you know about the dwarven expedition?” (Depends on story progress)
"Dwarves? Aye. Had my forge busy near every day for a week. Came with coin and questions. Iron seams, old mines, smelting in cursed ground. Sounded like miners to me." Ronan shrugs.
"One of 'em kept asking about old forges, runes stamped into tools, weapons no one's made in generations. Serious sort. Didn't look like a man chasing stories."
"Then they headed west into Duskhollow. Didn't expect to see 'em again. Truth be told, I still don't."
"So you found the dwarves after all?" Ronan grunts. "Good. Was starting to think the woods had eaten the lot of them."
You place the note on Aldren's desk. He reads it quickly and taps his wooden leg with irritation.
"A dragon, eh? Hah. Figures. Around here it's never wolves, bandits, or bad weather. Always has to be a damned dragon."
"Whatever they're after, they're stubborn enough to keep going. Dwarves usually are. If anyone can drag a half-dead expedition to the finish line, it's their kind."
Choose “Do you ever make enchanted weapons?”
"You want glowy things? Talk to Khelebar. Me? I make steel that doesn't snap when you need it most." He grins. "Which, frankly, is the real magic."
Choose “Trade” (Received Ronan’s mission to find a helmet, The helmet has not been found yet, Missing Helm of the Barbarian)
"No hard feelings. But no trade either. Bring me my helmet. Then we'll talk."
Choose “Trade” (According to “Heart of the Barbarian” Task progress, Missing Helm of the Barbarian)
"No hard feelings. But no trade either. Bring me steel that remembers its maker. Then we'll talk."
Choose “Trade” (Quests “Heart of the Barbarian” Not yet appeared)
"Trade, huh? Thought so."
Subsequent dialogue (Defeating the enemy (Armored Orc Fighter))
"Well, perfect. A mastermind behind the orcs. That is exactly what we needed."
"Problem is, you're late to the fire. Iron's near gone, charcoal's worse. What little I've got, I keep for those spilling blood to keep this place standing." His eyes narrow, measuring the party.
"Still... lend a hand, and maybe I find something worth heating the forge for."
What kind of help?
Choose “Trade” (Received Ronan’s mission to find a helmet, The helmet has not been found yet, Holding Helm of the Barbarian)
"You actually found it?"
He takes the helmet gently, turning it in his hands. A long pause.
"Still smells like smoke and pine sap. Gods... I didn't think I'd see it again."
"You've got my thanks. And my forge. It is open now."
"If there's anything left in this cursed place worth shaping, I'll shape it for you."
Choose “Trade” (According to “Heart of the Barbarian” Task progress, Holding Helm of the Barbarian)
"Someone clever enough to point them at us and too much of a coward to sign a real name."
Choose “What kind of help?” (Quests “Heart of the Barbarian” Not yet appeared, Missing Helm of the Barbarian)
"Simple. I lost something. Old helmet. Nothing grand. Just steel and sweat. Mine."
"Left it west of Fangroot. One of the old hunting trails. Storm hit hard. Shadows moved faster. Didn't wait to see which came first."
"You bring it back, and I'll make sure you get a fair deal at my forge."
Alright. We'll look for your helmet.
Why not fetch it yourself?
Choose “What kind of help?” (Quests “Heart of the Barbarian” Not yet appeared, Holding Helm of the Barbarian)
You mean this helmet?
Choose “You mean this helmet?”
Choose “Alright. We'll look for your helmet.”
He sets the paper aside, jaw tight. "We cannot act on this yet. There is nothing solid to work with."
"Find it, and you'll have more than my thanks. You'll have my forge." He nods once, sharp and final, then turns back to the fire.
Choose “Why not fetch it yourself?”
He pauses, hammer halfway to the anvil. His jaw tightens. "Let's just say I don't keep fond memories of that place."
"There's a tree out there. Dead and twisted, standing all alone. Reminded me of an old story. One where the hero didn't walk away."

Warm, smoky light falls on the rough wooden beams and the crooked stool. The air carries the smell of damp wood, aged barley wine, and some faint herbal scent. Tiled cups fill the table, some half-full, some long forgotten.

A large man stands behind the counter. Bearded, broad-shouldered, with a stained apron and a green cap. He wipes his hands on a rag and watches you with a knowing smile, like he's seen your kind before.
Suspended from a hook above the bar swings a heavy iron cage. Inside sits a black bird with a crooked wing and a glowing red eye. It blinks slowly, then croaks in a dry, mocking tone a crude insult.
The barkeep just chuckles and reaches for another mug. "Welcome to The Crooked Wing. Ale's warm, beds are dry, and supplies won't sell themselves."

The door creaks open again. The same crooked beams, The same smell of smoke. On the rafters, That bird moved slightly on the tree branch, A red eye flashed. The boss nodded lightly.
“Back again? Probably not enough luck... or not enough food.”
Select “Back” / “We've changed our minds.”
"But you can. Find this M. When you know who it is, finish it."
Buy supplies
Chat
Sleep (Cost 10 gold)
Choose “Chat”
"Got questions, huh? Fine. Talk and drink fast."
What's wrong with that raven?
We received a letter offering work.
Where can we buy gear?
Choose “What's wrong with that raven?”
"That thing? It's always been here. Came with the tavern, far as anyone knows. Old Garrel tried to shut it in a cage once. Lost three fingers and most of his teeth."
He rubs his temple, tired but steady. "The orcs are gone thanks to you. Now find the one who pushed them."
"Another fellow slipped poison in its feed. They found him face-down in a barrel of pickled eggs, feathers in his mouth."

"Truth is, the bird's half the reason this place is still known outside the village. Folks come just to hear it scream at strangers. So... I give it a perch, and it lets me sleep at night. Fair trade."

"Oh, I remember them well. Dwarves drink like dying camels. Took three barrels in two nights, and still wanted more. One of 'em swore he could outdrink the raven. Nearly did." He chuckles, then lowers his voice.
"Funny thing though, for all the talk of gold and treasure, they had a priest with them. Barely touched his drink. Never seen dwarf quite like him." He shrugs. "Some kind of fanatic, I'd wager."
"West they went. And west they stayed. Not the kind of tale you end with a toast."
"You found them?" The innkeeper visibly brightens. "Well, that's good news."
"Good folk, those dwarves. Tell them they're welcome back anytime."
Choose “We received a letter offering work.”
"M?" The innkeeper bursts into laughter. "What's with you? You're the third group recently asking the very same thing."
"Never heard of anyone around here hiring adventurers. Sounds like some kind of prank if you ask me."
Choose “Leave conversation” (Repelled the half-orcs that attacked the village, Quests “Bells of Underkeep” Completed)
"If you're looking for honest work, though, go see Mayor Aldren. Trust me, he'll find something."
Choose “Where can we buy gear?”
"Gear? Depends what kind you're after. Ronan the blacksmith's got his forge just across the way. Won't say much, but his blades hold better than most adventurers."
"Barlo's your man for everything else. Sells anything you need, and twice as much you don't. If it rattles, glows, or smells funny, he's probably got it."
"And if you're bleeding or growing a third eye, pay a visit to old Khelebar. Local healer... alchemist... whatever he is these days."
Choose “Buy supplies”
"Nothing worse than being on the road without food, eh? Take a look."
Choose “Sleep (Cost 10 gold)”
"Luxury, privacy, and probably no rats. Only ten gold."
Pay 10 gold.
Is there anything else weighing on you? (once only)
We've changed our minds.
Choose “Pay 10 gold.” (Have at least 10 gold coins)
"Room's yours. Fresh sheets too. Fresher than most, at least," he says, cracking a tired smile.
"Sleep well... "
Choose “Pay 10 gold.” (Fewer than 10 gold coins)
"Ten coins," he repeats. "Not eight. Not 'I'll pay you later.' Ten."
"Try to come back in one piece."
The muddy path leads you into Underkeep, a small village huddled beneath the darkening sky. Cold rain falls steadily over the rooftops.
Old wooden houses line the narrow streets. Their roofs sag under years of neglect, and thick mud clings to your boots. The air smells of wet timber and rotting fish.
Smoke curls weakly from chimneys, swallowed by mist. Once a stop for treasure seekers and fools chasing myths, now it rots slowly beneath the drops, sinking year by year into the wet earth.
About that bracelet. (Task "Where the Howls Fell Silent" is in progress.)
Choose “We have some questions.”
Tell us about the village.
When you return to the mayor's house, the chaos has ebbed. Smoke curls from the distant rooftops, and the alarm bells have gone silent at last.
You used to be an adventurer?
What happened to your leg?
Ask about the dwarven expedition. (once only)
Leave conversation
Choose “Is there anything else weighing on you?”
"Bandits are gone. Orcs are licking their wounds. Underkeep is quiet." A pause.
"So now I am going to ask you for something I would not ask a guard."
His gaze drifts aside for a heartbeat, not to any place in the room, but somewhere further back.
"I lost a bracelet." His voice stays flat, but his eyes do not.
"It is out on the wolf territory. Somewhere the sane do not go unless they have to."
Mayor Aldren stands near the doorway, his coat torn and his face streaked with soot. He exhales slowly as he sees you.
"But if there is anyone in this village reckless enough to walk in and walk out, it is you."
"If you cross that territory and happen to find it... I would appreciate you bringing it back."
Why is the bracelet so important?
We will look for it.
Not our problem.
Choose “Why is the bracelet so important?”
Aldren is silent for a moment. His fingers tighten around the cane.
"It belonged to someone close to me."
"We were caught in a wolf hunt gone wrong. Too many of them. I was slow. Already bleeding."
"She stayed behind so I could run. Bought me time. Bought me my life."
"So it's done, then?" he asks, voice rough from shouting.
"I lost the leg that night. She paid the rest."
"The bracelet was a gift. A small thing. It's all I have left of her."
Choose “We will look for it.”
Aldren nods once. No speech. Just a quiet relief he tries to hide.
"Good." He clears his throat.
"Follow the trail and do what you do."
Choose “Not our problem.”
Aldren does not argue. He only looks away, jaw tight for a heartbeat.
"Fair." He taps his wooden leg once. "I have asked worse of better men."
Choose “About that bracelet.” (Without Amulet of Remembrance)
"You've done well. Better than most of my guards, frankly."
"Wolf territory." He says it like a warning and a reminder.
"If you find it, bring it to me. Not the inn. Not the market. Me."
Choose “About that bracelet.” (With Amulet of Remembrance)
You place the bracelet into his hands. For a moment, Aldren does not react at all.
Then his fingers close around it, careful, almost reverent. As if the memory itself might break.
"Thank you." His voice is low, steady only because he forces it.
He looks up at you, eyes tired, honest.
"I don't know how to repay a thing like this."
"I have little left to give."
He nods toward your party.

Completed “Rag Doll Run” After that…, Choose “Got any new quest?”→“We'll find them.”

Select "About those mushrooms...", give them to Barlo, and you will earn 400 XP and 40 gold coins. You will also receive recipes for two types of mushroom stews and Dungeon Toast, along with a portion of Dungeon Toast.
If you return the five mushrooms to the Swampling, you will complete the quest "The Five Lost" and fail Barlo's mission.
maps.points.village_of_underkeep.e07.que: Select "Chat" → "Do you know anything about the Dwarf Expedition Team?" You will learn that they inquired about old mines and furnaces, and later moved westward into Duskhollow Woods.
Choose “Trade”→“What kind of help?”→“Alright. We'll look for your helmet.”
Retrieve the Helm of the Barbarian
Follow the old trail on the west side of Fangroot Forest, and near the isolated twisted trees, find the "Helm of the Barbarian".

Bring the helmet back, and select "Trade" to return it. If you brought the helmet when you first approached, you can directly select "Are you referring to this helmet?". Both methods will earn you 400 XP and unlock Ronan's weapon store.
maps.points.village_of_underkeep.e08.que: Select "Chat" → "We have received a letter offering a job." The shopkeeper will mention that other people have also come with letters, and will guide you to find Mayor Aldren to accept the mission.
In the "Chat" section, select "Do you know anything about the Dwarf Expedition?" to learn that the expedition left the village to the west.
Asking about the Dwarf Expedition team yields 120 XP.
maps.points.village_of_underkeep.e09.que: Choose "We have some questions." → "What about the Dwarf Expedition team?" This reveals that the expedition headed west towards Duskhollow Woods, with the priests on the team searching for ancient dwarf relics.
After rescuing Jacob, inquire about the "Source?" with him in the tomb. Go to Chambers of Endless Sleep to defeat the guards, then choose "End it." Destroy the source.
Return to the village and speak with Khelebar. Choose "We destroyed the source." This grants 400 XP.
You can choose this option during the initial conversation “Can we help with something?”→“Sounds good enough.”

Investigate the broken steles northwest of "Depths of the Broken Seal," and then copy the obelisks located in the northeastern Druid forest, the southwestern hidden area, and the southeastern half of the orc camp, all belonging to "Roots of Underkeep."
Scour the surroundings and select "Regarding those obelisks." You will earn 400 XP, 30 gold coins, and a Teleportation Stone. The Teleportation Stone can be used to activate the Roadstone.
First, investigate Jacob’s cottage in the Fangroot Forest and read the letter he left behind.
Go to Khelebar and select "We have some questions." → "Do you know Jacob?" → "He mentioned you in his letter." Obtain the Ring of Corpsebane, and continue with "Shadows of the South."
If Jacob is rescued before returning, you can directly select "We have rescued Jacob." You will receive 1000 XP and an Amulet of the Sage. This reward can only be obtained once.
Follow Khelebar’s clues to the Underkeep Cemetery in the south of the village. Enter the cemetery and rescue Jacob from the Cells of the Forgotten.
Return to the village and select "We have some questions." → "We have rescued Jacob." You will receive 1000 XP and an Amulet of the Sage.
maps.points.village_of_underkeep.f01.det: After completing “Echoes in the North”, visit the village chief at (11, -11) and choose “Do you have any other matters that require our assistance?”. When the alarm rings and “Bells of Underkeep” is triggered, half-orcs will appear near the western gate.
